text:
alex: Heads up — saw a small latency regression on short requests after the kernel routing change. 95p latency up ~12% on s1-small-prefill trace.
maria: Can you paste the exact numbers / trace id?
alex: Sure, snippet from profiling run:```
trace_id: s1-prefill-2026-03-16
qps: 1200
95p_prefill_latency: 42ms -> 47ms (+11.9%)
avg_decode_latency: 8ms (unchanged)
short_request_ratio (<64 tokens): 36%
```
sam: Link to dashboard? https://perf.redwood/company/eng-runtime/trace/s1-prefill-2026-03-16
alex: Linked. tl;dr: regression correlates with last kernel-routing PR that touched split heuristics.
jin: Hypothesis: `split_threshold_tokens` was bumped 8 -> 16 in that PR; that delays stage separation so many short requests stay in the prefill batch and end up on a different kernel path (bigger GEMM), increasing tail latency.
maria: I also saw KV-cache churn — there are extra KV drain/warm events near the same timestamps.
dev-bot: nightly-profile-1905120000 completed: hot_kernels: [block_gemm_f32, small_gemm_q8]; note: block_gemm_f32 shows higher memory stalls on these traces.
sam: Suggestion: run a small A/B: lower `split_threshold_tokens` back to 6 on one canary pool and keep kernel-routing changes. measure 95p for short requests.
alex: I spun a staging canary with this config (nodepool=fast-prefill-canary). Config snippet:```json
{"inference": {"split_threshold_tokens": 6, "token_budget_target": 64, "phase_routing": true}}
```
maria: What about `token_budget_target`? If we lower it we force earlier split and smaller prefill batches. Might help latency at throughput cost.
jin: Current `token_budget_target` is 64 in prod. Lowering to 32 could reduce prefill batch sizes for high short-request mixes. Also tweak kernel_selector to prefer `small_matmul` for seq_len <= 48.
sam: Can we run microbench on a node with synthetic short payloads to get controlled numbers?
alex: Yep, launched a microbench job against fast-prefill-canary (job id mb-190512).
maria: I pushed a quick alert `splitpoint_evictions` to catch cases where we repeatedly re-route a request between stages.
dev-bot: microbench mb-190512 started (workers=8, qps=200).
alex: Early canary numbers: 95p down ~5% after setting `split_threshold_tokens=6` + kernel selector tweak. Throughput dropped ~3% for that pool.
maria: Good signal. Can you get profile flame for the canary run?
jin: Attaching profiling notes: kernel selector log shows more hits on `small_matmul_q8` for seq<=48 after change. KV drain events drop by ~20%. Means less cache churn.
sam: Next step: try token_budget_target=40 as middle ground. Also keep a stable fallback: if prefill > 128 tokens then force decode split to avoid worst-case tails.
alex: Created PR with the A/B config + fallback rule: https://git.redwood/p/r/8245 — canary deploy queued.
maria: Assign owners: alex (canary runs + dashboards), jin (kernel selector patch), sam (rollout), i'll monitor alerts. :thumbsup:
alex: Canary finished — deploy-bot reports: `deploy-bot: canary completed on 3/3 nodes`. Observed 95p improvement ~6% and throughput loss ~2% aggregated.
maria: Let's run one more with `token_budget_target=40` and compare cost model. If latency improvement justifies small throughput hit we can roll.
jin: I'll prepare an experiment matrix: [split_threshold: 6,8,10] x [token_budget: 32,40,64] x [kernel_pref_threshold: 48,64]. Will run overnight and post results.
sam: Remember to include regression test in perf-suite for short-request mix so this doesn't regress silently.
alex: Adding `short-request-95p` check to nightly perf (threshold 5% delta).
maria: Also document the knobs in eng-runtime README under "phase-split heuristics" (short blurb + safe defaults).
alex: Drafted doc snippet and pushed to docs branch in the repo.
jin: One risk: for long prefix sequences we might over-split and increase total tokens processed. We'll add metric `split_extra_tokens` to monitor bytes-of-overhead.
sam: Good call. Also add an alert when `kv_warm_rate` increases >15% over baseline.
alex: OK — tracking board updated. I'll post final numbers tomorrow morning after the full matrix completes.
maria: Thanks all, great triage loop. We'll aim to roll the split_threshold + kernel selector together once metrics are stable. :rocket:
